1. `BivvyConfig` uses `#[serde(default)]` at the struct level, meaning all unknown/misnamed fields are silently ignored
2. There's no `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on any config struct
3. When a user has a typo in their config (e.g., `stpes` instead of `steps`, or `commmand` instead of `command`), serde silently ignores the unknown field and uses the default value

The fix:
1. Add `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` to `BivvyConfig`, `Settings`, `StepConfig`, `WorkflowConfig`, `StepOverride`, `WorkflowSettings`, `EnvironmentConfig`, `StepEnvironmentOverride` - essentially all the structs that have `#[serde(default)]` to indicate they accept partial configs


2. The config loading pipeline first deserializes raw YAML into `serde_yaml::Value` for merging, then parses the merged result into `BivvyConfig`, so the `deny_unknown_fields` check will catch typos at that final deserialization step. The direct parsing paths in `parse_config` and `load_config_file` will also benefit from this change.
3. I need to check the existing test that validates empty configs get proper defaults to make sure adding this constraint doesn't break it.

When the input is `null` (which is what an empty YAML string becomes), serde should still apply the struct defaults even with `deny_unknown_fields` enabled, since `null` has no fields to reject. The key thing is that `deny_unknown_fields` only triggers when there's an actual field mismatch, not when the input is empty or null.    - `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` attribute to reject unknown/mistyped field names
